entries.title: Birth of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ
entries.summary: Birth in Makkah.
entries.detailed_information: Known as the Year of the Elephant.

entries.title: First Revelation
entries.summary: Angel Jibril reveals the first verses of the Quran at Cave Hira.
entries.detailed_information: Marked the beginning of prophethood.

entries.title: Beginning of Public Preaching
entries.summary: The Prophet begins public preaching at Mount Safa.
entries.detailed_information: Led to intense opposition from the Quraysh leaders.

entries.title: First Migration to Abyssinia
entries.summary: A group of Muslims migrates to seek refuge under the Christian King Negus.
entries.detailed_information: A crucial strategic move to escape severe persecution.

entries.title: Year of Sorrow
entries.summary: Death of Abu Talib and Khadijah.
entries.detailed_information: The loss of his primary protector and beloved wife severely affected the Prophet.

entries.title: Journey to Ta'if
entries.summary: The Prophet travels to Ta'if seeking support but is violently rejected.
entries.detailed_information: A profound test of patience and resilience.

entries.title: Isra and Mi'raj
entries.summary: The Night Journey to Jerusalem and ascension to the Heavens.
entries.detailed_information: A miraculous event where the daily prayers (Salah) were prescribed.

entries.title: First Pledge of Aqabah
entries.summary: Delegation from Yathrib accepts Islam.
entries.detailed_information: Paved the way for the eventual migration (Hijrah).

entries.title: Second Pledge of Aqabah
entries.summary: 73 men and 2 women from Yathrib pledge to protect the Prophet.
entries.detailed_information: Solidified the political alliance necessary for the Hijrah.

entries.title: The Hijrah (Migration)
entries.summary: The Prophet and his companions migrate to Yathrib (Madinah).
entries.detailed_information: Marks the beginning of the Islamic calendar.

entries.title: Constitution of Madinah
entries.summary: Drafting of a constitution uniting the tribes of Madinah.
entries.detailed_information: Established the first Islamic state with rights for both Muslims and Jews.

entries.title: Battle of Badr
entries.summary: The first major battle between Muslims and Quraysh.
entries.detailed_information: A decisive victory for the heavily outnumbered Muslims.

entries.title: Battle of Uhud
entries.summary: The second major encounter with the Quraysh.
entries.detailed_information: Resulted in a tactical setback and the martyrdom of Hamza.

entries.title: Battle of the Trench (Khandaq)
entries.summary: Muslims successfully defend Madinah against a massive confederate army.
entries.detailed_information: Used a strategic trench suggested by Salman al-Farsi.

entries.title: Treaty of Hudaybiyyah
entries.summary: A 10-year peace treaty signed with the Quraysh.
entries.detailed_information: Allowed a period of peace that led to massive expansion of Islam.

entries.title: Conquest of Khaybar
entries.summary: Muslims capture the fortified oasis of Khaybar.
entries.detailed_information: Secured the northern flank of Madinah.

entries.title: Battle of Mu'tah
entries.summary: First major encounter with Byzantine forces.
entries.detailed_information: A grueling battle where Khalid ibn al-Walid saved the Muslim army from annihilation.

entries.title: Conquest of Makkah
entries.summary: The peaceful surrender of Makkah to the Prophet.
entries.detailed_information: The idols in the Kaaba were destroyed and a general amnesty was declared.

entries.title: Year of Delegations
entries.summary: Tribes from across Arabia send delegations to accept Islam.
entries.detailed_information: Islam becomes the dominant force in the Arabian Peninsula.

entries.title: Farewell Pilgrimage and Death
entries.summary: The Prophet delivers his Farewell Sermon and passes away shortly after.
entries.detailed_information: Completed the revelation of the Quran.

entries.title: Election of Abu Bakr
entries.summary: Abu Bakr is chosen as the first Caliph at Saqifah.
entries.detailed_information: Maintained unity immediately following the Prophet's death.

entries.title: Ridda Wars Begin
entries.summary: Abu Bakr campaigns against rebel tribes that committed apostasy or refused Zakat.
entries.detailed_information: Solidified state control over the Arabian Peninsula.

entries.title: Battle of Yamama
entries.summary: Decisive battle against the false prophet Musaylimah.
entries.detailed_information: The high number of Huffaz (Quran memorizers) killed prompted the compilation of the Quran.

entries.title: Compilation of the Quran
entries.summary: Zayd ibn Thabit is commissioned to compile a single written copy of the Quran.
entries.detailed_information: Ensured the preservation of the text.

entries.title: Campaigns in Iraq & Syria Begin
entries.summary: Muslim armies engage the Sassanid and Byzantine empires.
entries.detailed_information: Initiated the rapid expansion of the Caliphate.

entries.title: Death of Abu Bakr & Election of Umar
entries.summary: Umar ibn al-Khattab becomes the second Caliph.
entries.detailed_information: Marked the beginning of massive administrative and territorial expansion.

entries.title: Battle of Yarmouk
entries.summary: Decisive victory over the Byzantine Empire.
entries.detailed_information: Secured the Levant for the Caliphate.

entries.title: Battle of al-Qadisiyyah
entries.summary: Decisive victory over the Sassanid Persian Empire.
entries.detailed_information: Led to the fall of Iraq to the Muslims.

entries.title: Conquest of Jerusalem
entries.summary: Patriarch Sophronius surrenders Jerusalem to Caliph Umar.
entries.detailed_information: Umar guarantees the safety of Christian holy sites.

entries.title: Conquest of Ctesiphon
entries.summary: The Sassanid capital falls to Muslim forces.
entries.detailed_information: Marked the effective end of the Sassanid imperial government.

entries.title: Conquest of Egypt
entries.summary: Amr ibn al-As captures Alexandria.
entries.detailed_information: Added a major agricultural and economic powerhouse to the empire.

entries.title: Battle of Nahavand
entries.summary: Known as the "Victory of Victories" against the Persians.
entries.detailed_information: Resulted in the complete collapse of the Sassanid military.

entries.title: Assassination of Umar
entries.summary: Caliph Umar is assassinated by a Persian slave.
entries.detailed_information: A devastating loss for the Muslim community.

entries.title: Election of Uthman
entries.summary: Uthman ibn Affan is elected by a shura council.
entries.detailed_information: The empire continued its vast economic and territorial expansion.

entries.title: Standardization of the Quran
entries.summary: Uthman orders standard copies of the Quran to be distributed.
entries.detailed_information: Prevented dialectical variations from causing division.

entries.title: Battle of the Masts
entries.summary: First major naval victory for the Muslims against the Byzantines.
entries.detailed_information: Established Islamic naval supremacy in the eastern Mediterranean.

entries.title: Assassination of Uthman
entries.summary: Rebels lay siege to Uthman's house and assassinate him.
entries.detailed_information: Ignited the First Fitna (Civil War).

entries.title: Election of Ali & Battle of the Camel
entries.summary: Ali becomes Caliph but faces opposition regarding Uthman's killers.
entries.detailed_information: Resulted in the first major battle between Muslim factions.

entries.title: Battle of Siffin
entries.summary: Ali's forces clash with Mu'awiyah's Syrian army.
entries.detailed_information: Ended in controversial arbitration that split Ali's supporters.

entries.title: Assassination of Ali
entries.summary: Ali is assassinated by a Kharijite.
entries.detailed_information: Marks the end of the Rashidun Caliphate.

entries.title: Hasan-Mu'awiyah Treaty
entries.summary: Hasan ibn Ali abdicates in favor of Mu'awiyah.
entries.detailed_information: Ends the First Fitna and establishes the Umayyad dynasty.

entries.title: Capital moved to Damascus
entries.summary: Mu'awiyah shifts the center of power from Kufa to Damascus.
entries.detailed_information: Brought the administration closer to Byzantine organizational models.

entries.title: Succession of Yazid
entries.summary: Mu'awiyah appoints his son Yazid as successor.
entries.detailed_information: Broke the tradition of consultative succession, sparking outrage.

entries.title: Tragedy of Karbala
entries.summary: Husayn ibn Ali and his family are massacred.
entries.detailed_information: A defining moment of resistance against tyranny.

entries.title: Battle of al-Harra
entries.summary: Umayyad forces sack Madinah to crush a rebellion.
entries.detailed_information: Deepened the unpopularity of the Umayyad rulers.

entries.title: Siege of Makkah
entries.summary: Umayyad army besieges Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr.
entries.detailed_information: The Kaaba is heavily damaged in the fighting.

entries.title: Accession of Abd al-Malik
entries.summary: Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan becomes Caliph.
entries.detailed_information: Consolidated the fractured empire during the Second Fitna.

entries.title: Construction of the Dome of the Rock
entries.summary: Abd al-Malik completes the Dome of the Rock.
entries.detailed_information: One of the oldest extant works of Islamic architecture.

entries.title: End of the Second Fitna
entries.summary: Al-Hajjaj besieges Makkah and defeats Ibn al-Zubayr.
entries.detailed_information: Restored undisputed Umayyad control over the empire.

entries.title: Arabization of Administration
entries.summary: Arabic made the official language of government registers.
entries.detailed_information: Minted the first purely Islamic dinars.

entries.title: Conquest of Carthage
entries.summary: Hassan ibn al-Nu'man captures Carthage from Byzantines.
entries.detailed_information: Secured North Africa for the Umayyads.

entries.title: Conquest of Transoxiana
entries.summary: Qutayba ibn Muslim begins campaigns in Central Asia.
entries.detailed_information: Expanded the empire to the borders of China.

entries.title: Conquest of Sindh
entries.summary: Muhammad bin Qasim conquers the Sindh region.
entries.detailed_information: Introduced Islam to the Indian subcontinent.

entries.title: Conquest of Al-Andalus
entries.summary: Tariq ibn Ziyad crosses into Spain.
entries.detailed_information: The beginning of 800 years of Islamic presence in Iberia.

entries.title: Siege of Constantinople
entries.summary: Massive land and sea siege of the Byzantine capital.
entries.detailed_information: The siege failed, halting Islamic expansion into Eastern Europe.

entries.title: Reforms of Umar II
entries.summary: Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz initiates sweeping egalitarian reforms.
entries.detailed_information: Abolished unfair taxes on non-Arab converts (Mawali).

entries.title: Battle of Toulouse
entries.summary: Al-Samh ibn Malik is defeated by Odo of Aquitaine.
entries.detailed_information: A significant check on Umayyad expansion in Francia.

entries.title: Battle of Tours (Poitiers)
entries.summary: Charles Martel defeats the Umayyad army.
entries.detailed_information: Halted major Islamic incursions into Western Europe.

entries.title: Great Berber Revolt
entries.summary: Berbers rebel against discriminatory Umayyad policies.
entries.detailed_information: Permanently fractured Umayyad control in North Africa.

entries.title: Abbasid Revolution & Battle of the Zab
entries.summary: The Abbasids definitively crush the Umayyad army.
entries.detailed_information: Caliph Marwan II is killed, ending the Umayyad Caliphate in the East.

entries.title: Establishment of the Abbasid Caliphate
entries.summary: Abu al-Abbas al-Saffah is proclaimed Caliph.
entries.detailed_information: Marked a shift towards a more inclusive, cosmopolitan Islamic empire.

entries.title: Founding of Baghdad
entries.summary: Al-Mansur builds the Round City.
entries.detailed_information: Became the world's center of wealth and knowledge.

entries.title: Reign of Harun al-Rashid
entries.summary: The zenith of Abbasid political and cultural power.
entries.detailed_information: Immortalized in the 1001 Nights.

entries.title: Fall of the Barmakids
entries.summary: Harun al-Rashid purges the powerful Barmakid vizier family.
entries.detailed_information: A brutal consolidation of absolute caliphal power.

entries.title: Fourth Fitna (Civil War)
entries.summary: War between brothers Al-Amin and Al-Ma'mun over succession.
entries.detailed_information: Resulted in massive destruction in Baghdad and Al-Ma'mun's victory.

entries.title: House of Wisdom Expansion
entries.summary: Al-Ma'mun patronizes the massive translation movement.
entries.detailed_information: Greek philosophy and science are heavily translated into Arabic.

entries.title: The Mihna (Inquisition)
entries.summary: Al-Ma'mun enforces the Mu'tazilite doctrine of the created Quran.
entries.detailed_information: Ahmad ibn Hanbal is famously tortured for refusing to agree.

entries.title: Founding of Samarra
entries.summary: Al-Mu'tasim moves the capital to Samarra.
entries.detailed_information: To house his new, powerful Turkic slave-soldier army (Mamluks).

entries.title: Anarchy at Samarra
entries.summary: Turkic guards assassinate Caliph Al-Mutawakkil.
entries.detailed_information: Initiated a decade of severe political instability.

entries.title: Zanj Rebellion
entries.summary: A massive slave revolt in southern Iraq.
entries.detailed_information: Severely drained Abbasid resources and lasted 14 years.

entries.title: Rise of the Buyids
entries.summary: Shi'a Buyid emirs take control of Baghdad.
entries.detailed_information: The Abbasid Caliph became merely a figurehead under their control.

entries.title: Fatimid Conquest of Egypt
entries.summary: Fatimids establish Cairo and Al-Azhar.
entries.detailed_information: A direct challenge to Abbasid religious authority.

entries.title: Seljuk Turks Capture Baghdad
entries.summary: Tughril Beg drives out the Buyids.
entries.detailed_information: Sunni orthodoxy is championed, but the caliph remains politically weak.

entries.title: Establishment of Al-Nizamiyya
entries.summary: Nizam al-Mulk founds a network of Sunni madrasas.
entries.detailed_information: Formalized higher Islamic education and countered Shi'a influence.

entries.title: Battle of Manzikert
entries.summary: Seljuks crush the Byzantine army.
entries.detailed_information: Opened the doors for Turkish migration into Anatolia.

entries.title: First Crusade captures Jerusalem
entries.summary: Crusaders massacre the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
entries.detailed_information: Occurred during deep political fragmentation in the Muslim world.

entries.title: Salahuddin ends Fatimid Caliphate
entries.summary: Salahuddin restores Sunni allegiance in Egypt to the Abbasid Caliph.
entries.detailed_information: United Egypt and Syria under one front against the Crusaders.

entries.title: Battle of Hattin
entries.summary: Salahuddin recaptures Jerusalem.
entries.detailed_information: Effectively destroyed the Crusader Kingdom of Jerusalem.

entries.title: Mongol Sack of Baghdad
entries.summary: Hulagu Khan destroys Baghdad and executes the Caliph.
entries.detailed_information: The brutal end of the unified Abbasid Caliphate and the Golden Age.

entries.title: Re-establishment of Abbasids in Cairo
entries.summary: Mamluk Sultan Baibars installs an Abbasid survivor as Caliph in Cairo.
entries.detailed_information: Provided religious legitimacy to the Mamluk Sultanate.
